summary: Phase 5 Slice J (MS Graph dual-write to public.integrations) + Phase 6 (frontend defaults to Supabase JWT with legacy toggle pill) verified GREEN end-to-end. Backend pytest: 21/21 PASS in test_iteration19_phase5j_phase6.py. (1) /api/auth/login with admin@healthguard.com / Admin@123 returns access_token + user.id=8f16fe69-... role=admin. (2) /api/auth/me with the legacy HS256 JWT returns the admin profile (UUID matches). (3) Supabase password grant POST {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with admin@healthguard.com / AdminPassword123! returns a valid 3-segment access_token. (4) /api/supabase/me with the Supabase ES256 JWT returns {user:{id=8f16fe69-..., email=admin@healthguard.com, role=admin}} — UUID matches the legacy Mongo one (Phase 2 dual-mode auth). (5) /api/auth/me ALSO accepts the Supabase JWT and returns the same admin profile (dual-mode validated). (6) /api/clients GET, POST(TEST_SliceJ Client), DELETE work with the Supabase JWT (status 200/201/200). (7) /api/caregivers GET returns the seeded list including caregiver_id=389b257d-...  (8) /api/assignments GET + POST(client/caregiver) + DELETE work. (9) /api/documents GET returns 50 rows; /api/documents/{id}/url returns an https Supabase signed URL containing '/storage/' for at least one doc (iteration over docs handles pointer-only seed rows). (10) /api/chat/threads GET requires auth (401 without) and returns list with Supabase JWT. (11) /api/policies/acknowledgments GET returns list; POST /api/policies/acknowledge with body {policy_id:<doc_id>} and DELETE /api/policies/acknowledge/{policy_id} both 200. (12) /api/training GET + POST(create) + POST/{id}/complete + DELETE/{id} full flow 200/200/200/200. (13) /api/onboarding?caregiver_id=389b257d-... returns a non-empty list/dict of steps. (14) /api/packets/share POST {caregiver_id, recipient_name, recipient_role:'caregiver', category:'caregiver_onboarding', title} returns 200 with token; GET /api/packets/{token} (no auth) returns 200. (15) /api/ms/status returns {configured:true, connected, schedule:'America/New_York ... 1st ...'}. (16) Slice J DUAL-WRITE VERIFIED: POST /api/ms/email-recipients {email_to:'TEST_phase5j@phcp-smoke.io'} returns {ok:true}; subsequent GET /api/ms/status reflects email_to in Mongo; direct asyncpg query against SUPABASE_DIRECT_URL confirms public.integrations row exists with provider='microsoft_graph' AND config->>'email_to'='TEST_phase5j@phcp-smoke.io'. (17) Slice J DUAL-DELETE VERIFIED: POST /api/ms/disconnect returns {ok:true}; GET /api/ms/status shows connected=false AND empty email_to (Mongo cleared); asyncpg query confirms public.integrations row with provider='microsoft_graph' is GONE (Postgres cleared). (18) /api/stats returns {total_clients, total_caregivers, total_documents, total_training, audit_readiness, pending_onboarding, ...} with positive counts (1 client / 12 caregivers / 50 docs). FRONTEND (Expo web, mobile 390x844): (A) Login screen renders with toggle pill testID='auth-mode-toggle' visible and reading 'Auth: Supabase · tap to switch' by default (Phase 6 default). (B) Default Supabase flow: admin@healthguard.com / AdminPassword123! -> router replaces to home and Dashboard renders 'AUDIT READINESS 51% / Action needed / Onboarding 2% / Training 100%' and OVERVIEW '1 Clients / 12 Caregivers / 50 Documents / 0 Trainings' with all 6 tabs (Dashboard, Documents, Team, Schedule, Policies, Assistant). (C) Logout button testID='logout-button' (top-right exit icon in header) is tappable and returns to /login. (D) On login, tapping the toggle pill flips it to 'Auth: Legacy (MongoDB) · tap to switch' AND the password field auto-fills to 'Admin@123' (Phase 6 quality-of-life). (E) Signing in with the legacy mode (admin@healthguard.com / Admin@123) returns to the same Dashboard (legacy JWT path). (F) Team tab shows 'Test Client Jones' under the Clients sub-tab and the Caregivers + Onboarding sub-tabs are also present. (G) Tapping the client navigates to /client/{id}; the detail screen renders the client name + photo + 'Tasks (13)', 'Schedule (3)', 'Care Team (1)' tabs with the 13 onboarding task rows listed.
action_items: (Optional / nice-to-have) The seed Mongo documents collection includes 12 pointer-only rows (file_base64=null AND no corresponding storage blob) that return 404 from /api/documents/{id}/url with 'No stored file for this document'. The Phase-4 doc API is correct (404 is the right response for missing object), but the UI may want to hide the 'download/view' affordance on rows where storage_path is absent so users don't tap into a guaranteed-404. Logs show 'core.supa_data - WARNING - [supa-storage] signed_url failed for documents/1c401eee-... Object not found' for those rows.

(Optional cosmetic) login.tsx prints the required-credentials hint at the bottom of the screen using non-Title-Case glyphs ('Supabase' with a lowercase 'p' inside the cred-hint card vs the toggle pill which says 'Supabase' capitalised). Not a bug, just spelling drift — happens in /app/frontend/app/(auth)/login.tsx (cred-hint footer text).

(Already known) passlib emits a benign warning at startup: 'module bcrypt has no attribute __about__'. This is the bcrypt 4.x + passlib mismatch and is suppressed in the (trapped) branch — it does NOT affect auth. Listed only for completeness.

(Already known) ngrok tunnel restarts occasionally; expo.err.log shows 'CommandError: ngrok tunnel took too long to connect.' historic entries — current tunnel is up and the preview URL responds 200, so no action needed.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/ms_graph.py:529-537 ms_disconnect — Mongo delete_one runs first, then supa_data.delete_integration is wrapped in try/except and only logs at WARNING. This is the correct best-effort design from Phase 5 Slice J: a Postgres outage cannot block the Mongo disconnect (legacy path stays authoritative).

routers/ms_graph.py:540-562 ms_email_recipients — same dual-write pattern: Mongo upsert first (db.integrations with _id='ms_connection'), then supa_data.upsert_integration_tokens(provider='microsoft_graph', tokens={}, config={'email_to':email_to}) wrapped in try/except. tokens={} is correct here because email-recipients does NOT touch refresh_token state; the JSONB merge in supa_data is `tokens = public.integrations.tokens || excluded.tokens` so an empty merge is a no-op on existing tokens. Verified directly via asyncpg.

core/supa_data.py:1181-1205 upsert_integration_tokens — ON CONFLICT (provider) DO UPDATE with JSONB-merge semantics (`config || excluded.config`). This means subsequent calls with partial config (e.g., {'last_export':{...}}) won't clobber email_to. Correct merge semantics for Slice J.

core/supa_data.py:1231-1237 delete_integration — DELETE FROM public.integrations WHERE provider=$1. Verified: after /api/ms/disconnect the row with provider='microsoft_graph' returns NULL via direct PG SELECT.

frontend/app/(auth)/login.tsx — toggle pill (testID='auth-mode-toggle') correctly flips state and auto-fills the password field with the corresponding mode's known cred. Default is Supabase mode (SUPABASE_CONFIGURED=true). The legacy/Supabase branch in onSubmit picks the correct SDK call: supabase.auth.signInWithPassword for Supabase mode and the legacy /api/auth/login POST for Legacy mode.

frontend/src/api/client.ts auto-attaches the Supabase token from supabase.auth.getSession() when a session exists, otherwise falls back to the legacy AsyncStorage token. This is the correct dual-mode order: a real Supabase session wins because /api/auth/me's verify_jwt path will recognise ES256 first via JWKS.

success_rate.backend: 100% (21/21 pytest cases): legacy login + /api/auth/me; Supabase password grant + /api/supabase/me + /api/auth/me dual-accept; clients CRUD; caregivers GET; assignments flow; documents list + signed URL (Supabase https); chat/threads auth + GET; policies acks + acknowledge + DELETE; training GET/POST/complete/DELETE; onboarding by caregiver_id; packets share + GET; /api/ms/status + Slice J dual-write to Postgres public.integrations verified via direct asyncpg query + Slice J dual-delete; /api/stats counts.
success_rate.frontend: 100% — Phase 6 toggle pill testID='auth-mode-toggle' visible defaulting to Supabase; Supabase login -> Dashboard (Audit Readiness 51%, 1 Client / 12 Caregivers / 50 Documents / 0 Trainings, all 6 tabs); logout via testID='logout-button' returns to /login; toggle pill flips to Legacy (MongoDB) and auto-fills password to Admin@123; legacy login returns to Dashboard; Team tab shows 'Test Client Jones' (Clients/Caregivers/Onboarding sub-tabs); tapping the client opens /client/{id} with photo + Tasks (13) + Schedule (3) + Care Team (1).

seed_data_creation: Test created 1 TEST_SliceJ Client (deleted same test), 1 assignment (deleted), 1 TEST_SliceJ Training (created+completed+deleted), 1 policy acknowledgment (created+deleted), 1 packet share (token persists, not deleted — same behaviour as the Slice H suite which leaves a 2-row packet history). MS Graph email_to was set to 'TEST_phase5j@phcp-smoke.io' and then cleared via /api/ms/disconnect — no residue in either Mongo db.integrations or Postgres public.integrations.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 5 Slice J and Phase 6 are GREEN. The MS Graph dual-write path lives at routers/ms_graph.py:540-562 (email-recipients) and 529-537 (disconnect); the helpers are core/supa_data.py upsert_integration_tokens / delete_integration / MS_PROVIDER='microsoft_graph'. The Postgres schema is public.integrations(provider unique, user_id, tokens jsonb, config jsonb, ...). Verification was done via direct asyncpg connect to SUPABASE_DIRECT_URL (from backend/.env) — the test imports SUPABASE_DIRECT_URL directly because the regular pgbouncer pooler at 6543 also works but the direct 5432 is preferred for one-off integrity probes. Phase 6 frontend changes are at /app/frontend/app/(auth)/login.tsx (toggle pill + auto-fill), /app/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx (session caching in AsyncStorage 'sbUserInfo', logout always signs out Supabase), /app/frontend/src/api/client.ts (auto-attaches Supabase token preferentially). The login screen's logout-button testID is on the header exit icon (data-testid='logout-button'). Reusable fixtures: base_url, admin_token, admin_headers (legacy HS256), supabase_admin_token, sb_admin_headers (Supabase ES256). Pydantic enum constraints worth remembering for next time: /api/packets/share requires recipient_role in ('client','caregiver') and category in ('client_onboarding','caregiver_onboarding'); /api/policies/acknowledge requires body field 'policy_id' (NOT 'document_id'). /api/stats returns 'total_clients/total_caregivers/total_documents/total_training/audit_readiness/pending_onboarding/onboarding_pct/training_pct' (no 'onboarding_done/total' fields).
rca_of_issue: No backend or frontend bugs discovered. Initial pytest run hit 4 test-side AssertionErrors (wrong field name 'document_id' for policy ack, missing recipient_name/recipient_role/category on packets, /api/stats key shape mismatch, and a pointer-only seed document) — all corrected in the test file. After the corrections the entire 21-case suite passed on the next run. Slice J dual-write/delete to Postgres public.integrations is reliable: the asyncpg integrity check between the API call and the PG row read consistently observes the JSONB config containing email_to and a clean delete after /api/ms/disconnect.
